1.1.text:
Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 12

The Family and/or Parents as referred to in Article 6 letters c and d, have full responsibility to prevent all forms of Violence and protect Women as members of the Family.

Article 16

1. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 14 shall consist of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, and Repatriation assistance.
2. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for Women Victims of Violence including victims of trafficking in persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, and Women Victims of sexual exploitation.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 21

1. Community participation in Women's Protection may take the form of:
a. provision of counseling regarding women's rights;
b. provision of skills training to support the Family economy;
c. establishment of community social institutions to assist Victims of Violence; and
d. reporting to the competent authority if Violence Against Women occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

Article 18

Further provisions regarding the procedures for prevention, protection services, and Recovery of Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Articles 13 through 17 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 24

1. The Regional Government shall evaluate the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for Women's Protection at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for Women's Protection for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement Protection for Women.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by to live is the right to life and the right to defend life and livelihood.

Letter b
What is meant by to have a family and continue descendants is the right to form a family and continue descendants through lawful marriage.

Letter c
What is meant by to develop oneself is to develop oneself through the fulfillment of basic needs and to obtain education and benefit from science and technology, arts and culture, in order to improve quality of life and for the welfare of humankind.

Letter d
What is meant by to obtain justice is to receive recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law.

Letter e
What is meant by personal freedom is to advance oneself in fighting for one's rights collectively to build society, nation and state.

Letter f
What is meant by sense of security is the right to protection of oneself, family, honor, dignity and property under one's control, as well as the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right.

Letter g
What is meant by welfare is to live prosperously physically and mentally, to have a place to live and obtain a good and healthy living environment, as well as the right to obtain health services.

Letter h
What is meant by to participate in government is to obtain equal opportunity in government.

Letter a

What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:

What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;

c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.

19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for Women Victims of Violence including victims of trafficking in persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, and Women Victims of sexual exploitation.

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 16

1. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 14 shall consist of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, and Repatriation assistance.
2. The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for Women Victims of Violence including victims of trafficking in persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, and Women Victims of sexual exploitation.

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter b

Letter c

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Rights of Women Victims of Violence

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for Women Victims of Violence including victims of trafficking in persons, Women in disaster-prone areas, Women workers, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, and Women Victims of sexual exploitation.

Letter d
What is meant by to obtain justice is to receive recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law.

Letter e
What is meant by personal freedom is to advance oneself in fighting for one's rights collectively to build society, nation and state.

Letter f
What is meant by sense of security is the right to protection of oneself, family, honor, dignity and property under one's control, as well as the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a basic right.

Letter g
What is meant by welfare is to live prosperously physically and mentally, to have a place to live and obtain a good and healthy living environment, as well as the right to obtain health services.

Letter h
What is meant by to participate in government is to obtain equal opportunity in government.

CHAPTER VII

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 21

1. Community participation in Women's Protection may take the form of:
a. provision of counseling regarding women's rights;
b. provision of skills training to support the Family economy;
c. establishment of community social institutions to assist Victims of Violence; and
d. reporting to the competent authority if Violence Against Women occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

Article 28

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that implement Protection for Women.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 18

Further provisions regarding the procedures for prevention, protection services, and Recovery of Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Articles 13 through 17 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Letter a What is meant by policy analysis is applied social research that is systematically prepared in order to know the substance of the policy so that information can be clearly known regarding the problems answered by the policy and the problems that may arise as a result of the implementation of the policy.

What is meant by advocacy is social, political and cultural action carried out in a planned, structured manner, and conducted collectively, involving various tactics including lobbying, campaigns, establishing coalitions, applying mass action pressure, as well as research used to change policy.

Letter g

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Article 12

The Family and/or Parents as referred to in Article 6 letters c and d, have full responsibility to prevent all forms of Violence and protect Women as members of the Family.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter a

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;

What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

c. establishment of community social institutions to assist Victims of Violence; and
d. reporting to the competent authority if Violence Against Women occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector, and mass media.

Article 5

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
What is meant by psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
What is meant by sexual violence as referred to in Article 15 letter c is caused by:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter d
What is meant by domestic neglect is caused by:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of women as wives in a reasonable manner, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by the husband, parents, guardian, or other party;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of women as wives as they should be, committed by the husband, parents, guardian or other party;
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or.
d. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting work.

Letter e
What is meant by Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Letter f
What is meant by Exploitation as referred to in Article 15 letter f is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bandung Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bandung.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Women are human beings of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law.
6. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against Women.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred.
9. Victim is a Woman who experiences suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim.
11. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals.
12. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman.
14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
15. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion, or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil, or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and Women.
16. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
17. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their region of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and child Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance.

Article 30

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Bandung Regency.
